context_blocks.text: # 2\. Executive Summary and Canonical System Statement

target_blocks.text:
DOCUMENT PURPOSE

A governed extraction of the v0.4.7 decisions that remain useful after the v0.5 Home and Away redesigns. The document preserves MEDIAN’s attention architecture, shared world-state doctrine, MEET authoring rules, and presentation safeguards while explicitly retiring incompatible 0.4.7 assumptions.
| **SOURCE BASIS**       | v0.4.7 Running Decisions; v0.5 Home Mode, Colony, and DWELL Specification; v0.5 Away Loop Rework; v0.5 Philosophical Specification   |
| **STATUS**             | Working specification for the structured v0.5 revision document                                            |
| **PRECEDENCE**         | When this document conflicts with a v0.5 system specification, the newer v0.5 specification leads          |
| **SCOPE BOUNDARY**     | Guest Citizen mechanics and species-specific Guest capability design are deferred to a dedicated v0.5 pass |

target_blocks.parent_heading: # 1\. Purpose, Precedence, and the v0.4.7 Cross-System Carryforward Name
target_blocks.text:
<!--@2¶1-->
“v0.4.7 Cross-System Carryforward” is the working name for the cross-system rulings first developed in the v0.4.7 Registers, Views, and Encounter Mode thread and retained after the v0.5 redesign. It is not a revival of v0.4.7 as active canon. It is a controlled salvage operation: keep the architectural decisions that make the new Home and Away specifications cohere; archive the assumptions those specifications have superseded.

target_blocks.parent_heading: # 1\. Purpose, Precedence, and the v0.4.7 Cross-System Carryforward Name
target_blocks.text:
<!--@2¶2-->
The original log was explicitly proposed rather than settled canon. This specification therefore does not preserve entries because they were marked SETTLED inside that log. It re-rules them against the v0.5 architecture.
| **Priority** | **Authority**                          | **Use**                                                                                                                       |
| 1            | v0.5 Philosophical Specification       | Defines the game’s governing thesis, Home/Away split, attachment-first base-building purpose, and five-Register architecture. |

| 2            | v0.5 Home Mode, Colony, and DWELL Specification                  | Leads all domestic economy, Readiness, Role, Place, Project, Home MEET, Quiet Equilibrium, and EMBODY questions.              |
| 3            | v0.5 Away Loop Rework                  | Leads Launch, Crossing, Field, Nodes, Away MEET, Exposure, Return, Stopover, and Homecoming questions.                        |
| 4            | Other dedicated v0.5 specifications    | Lead within their subjects, including Embodiment, Ecology, Manifestations, and future Guest Citizen work.                     |

| 5            | This v0.4.7 Cross-System Attention, Persistence, and World-State Carryforward | Provides shared attention, authoring, display, persistence, and world-state doctrine across the above systems.                |
| 6            | The v0.4.7 Running Decisions log       | Historical source and rationale only.                                                                                         |

REVISION MANDATE

No 0.4.7 rule survives merely by silence. Contradictory assumptions are named as superseded rather than quietly inherited.

target_blocks.parent_heading: # 2\. Executive Summary and Canonical System Statement
target_blocks.text:
<!--@3¶1-->
The v0.5 redesign gives MEDIAN two highly developed halves: DWELL makes sanctuary mechanically achievable at Colony scale, while TRAVEL / RISK / MEET expose particular Citizens to distance and consequence. The v0.4.7 Cross-System Carryforward decisions provide the connective tissue that makes those halves feel like one game.
- When continuous Register play remains continuous and when the game fixes attention through MEET.
- How one authored situation can manifest differently in Home and Away contexts without becoming two systems.

## Status and qualification handling

The source declares itself a working specification for controlled v0.4.7
carry-forward into v0.5, not a revival of v0.4.7 as active canon. Extraction
must preserve its explicit retained, revised, superseded, retired, provisional,
deferred, open, illustrative, and precedence qualifications without resolving
them.

## Media and exclusions

The registered Markdown contains no embedded media or media-associated caption.
Its tables and textual examples are ordinary source text, not media. External
artwork and alternate representations are excluded.

Document-control furniture, nonsemantic whitespace, source-position comments,
pure structural headings, and table delimiters use the established
source-agnostic dispositions.

## Extraction boundary

Extract only game-semantic evidence present in the registered Markdown. Do not
import or consult external sources or adjudicate cross-source authority. The
source's own lineage and precedence material remains source-bounded content in
its appropriate chunks.

Source-bounded candidate acceptance is not semantic acceptance, mapping,
reconciliation, canonization, compiled prose, or permission to begin another
source, later compile stage, or Google Sheets work.

## Approval boundary

Asa Wember approved this source identity and extraction boundary. Approval
permits the established Cross-System Carryforward-only offline preparation and
representative pilot calibration; provider readiness still requires validated
frozen bindings, completed offline and replay gates, sequential review, and
sufficient budget.

## Extraction contract

Separate claims only when each remains independently grounded and self-contained. Exact spans uniquely ground core assertions. Preserve coordinated subjects or effects in one atom when they share a predicate, subject, condition, or relationship
unless every split has a contiguous span containing its own subject and predicate. A subject or label alone never grounds an
imported predicate. Start each normalized claim with `exact_source_text`. For self-containment,
resolve pronouns and subjectless exact-text prefixes to explicit governing subjects; parent headings
may supply only necessary status or scope.
Never paraphrase, gloss, define, compare, infer, or complete implied meaning;
use `review_required` when necessary. Parent headings are context, never atoms. Every
`exact_source_text` is
a byte-for-byte contiguous target-block substring that occurs exactly once. After JSON decoding it contains actual target-block
characters, never literal backslash Unicode-escape spellings.
Expand repeated or nested terms with adjacent text until unique.
Include interrupting markup or split the atom.

Obey `required_disposition`, `allowed_dispositions`, and `minimum_atoms`;
`no_substantive_claim` requires empty `atoms`. Structural headings, labels, table headers,
delimiters, and document-control metadata carry no substantive atom. Never make
a label a tautological topic claim or use structural context to omit a
dependent substantive target.

For each substantive table row, cover every nonempty semantic cell. Separate
independent properties, functions, effects, examples, interpretations, stages,
actions, and results. Combine cells only when one qualifies
another or the relationship is indivisible. Preserve both endpoints of
categorical mappings.
Ground each headed cell under its header; never infer a relationship between
adjacent cells. No exact span crosses a semicolon; each side gets its own atom.
Copy every authored slash into the normalized claim; never replace it with a word unless the source defines that meaning.
Each independent table-cell assertion requires exact source text from its own
cell; never ground a ruling or consequence only in another cell.

Preserve provisional, historical, rejected, example, negative, conditional,
scope, ownership, and authority qualifiers. Use `review_required` instead of
guessing. Never repair source text or invent identifiers, statuses, owners, or
authorities.

## Output check

Return schema-bound JSON only after verifying exactly
`required_target_disposition_count` dispositions. Kind `atoms` requires nonempty
`atoms`; all other kinds require empty `atoms`. Every atom needs supplied source/target block IDs, an
allowed stream, exact source text, concise normalized claim, and source-faithful
claim kind. Derive each proposal ID from target block ID plus local atom ordinal;
proposal IDs must remain source-unique.
